- Windows 7 desktop: the File Explorer and the Control Panel are drawn the way Windows 7 draws them (round back and forward buttons, address bar, command bar, navigation pane; Control Panel in its Category view).
- Windows desktops: the caption buttons of Windows 7 are one glass pill with a red close button; the taskbar button of a window shows its progress; windows can be dragged to the right edge after the screen was turned; the icons of the old desktops have no tile behind them.
- Progress bars of Windows 95, XP and 7 are always drawn in their own style, with paused (yellow) and error (red) states.
- Game Hub: the delete button sits on the cover; with root an app is removed without Android's second question; a removed game leaves the shelf at once; the shelf rebuilds itself when it comes back blank.
- A crash offers a bug report on GitHub (a prefilled issue; nothing is sent by itself), in a window of Pulse's own look.
- Fix: a crash when the music player was opened in the launcher ("WorkManager is not initialized properly").
- Launcher: the wallpaper is no longer decoded at half size, so it is sharper.
- Music player: the wave seek bar can show the song's real waveform; the Poweramp look has a Blended cover (both options off by default).
- Keyboard: corner swipes (off by default); links and bits of code are never mended or split.
- Access per app: lifting a cut works, and a cut app shows a red slash.
- Keyboard: the suggestion bar keeps its height while nothing is suggested (a word the dictionary does not know), so the keys no longer jump up and down; only a field without suggestions (a password box, a number field) gives the room to the keys.
- Windows 7 look: the default wallpaper is the Windows 7 picture in two shapes, wide for a turned screen and a 9:16 cut from its middle for an upright one (before, an upright picture was stretched over a turned screen, which looked blurry).
